narration.full_text: Namaste, students! Welcome to our final quiz on Control and Coordination. This is your chance to consolidate everything we've learned. Are you ready? Let's begin! First question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief. Think about how auxins affect cell elongation. The answer is: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards, causing cell elongation. In tendrils, auxins move away from the contact point, leading to more growth on the opposite side, causing coiling. Next question: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant. Consider where auxins are formed and their role in different plant parts. The answer is: Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, it promotes cell enlargement and inhibits lateral bud development. In the root, it promotes cell division. Moving on: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support. Focus on growth dependence, speed, and direction. Here's the answer: Mimosa leaves show growth-independent, fast, non-directional movement. Tendrils show growth-dependent, slow, directional movement. And the final question: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants. (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement? Part (a) first: Name three plant hormones and their functions. The answer to part (a) is: Auxin promotes elongation and cell division. Gibberellins help in stem growth. Cytokinins promote cell division and delay leaf ageing. Now for part (b): How do plants move without muscles? The answer to part (b) is: Plants use electrical and chemical signals to convey information. Movements like Mimosa leaves folding are growth-independent, while a seedling breaking through soil is growth-dependent. Excellent work, everyone! I hope this quiz helped you review and solidify your understanding of Control and Coordination. Keep up the great learning!

verbatim_content.question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.
How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.
verbatim_content.answer: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards in the plant. These auxins cause cell elongation in the growing tissues. In the tendrils, auxins move away from the point of contact with the supporting object. More growth occurs on the side away from the support. As a result of unequal growth on the two sides, the tendril coils around the support.

verbatim_content.answer: Diagram illustrating the role of auxin in plant growth. Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, auxin promotes cell enlargement and inhibits the development of lateral buds. In the root, auxin promotes cell division.

verbatim_content.question:
(a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?
(a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
verbatim_content.answer:
(a) Three growth hormones in plants are-
(i) Auxin: It is synthesized in the young tip of roots and shoots. It promotes elongation and division of cell and root formation.
(ii) Gibberellins: They help in the growth of the stem.
(iii) Cytokinins: They promote cell division and delay leaf ageing.

verbatim_content.question: (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?
verbatim_content.answer: The ability of a plant to detect change and respond to that change is termed as the sensitivity of the plant. Yet plants have no nervous system and no muscle tissue, they use electrical and chemical means to convey the information from one cell to another cell. The leaves of the sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) folds up in response to touch. These leaf movements are independent of growth whereas, the directional movement of the shoot of a germinating seedling breaking through the soil is growth dependent.
